text.headline: Mean over 8-10 Hz and 1-2 mm tremor: ink error none 835 um, weighted 1000, pencil+AKF 694, Rev H+AKF as shipped 775, Rev H+AKF re-tuned 531, Rev H oracle 79; words read by the app 0.31 / 0.59 / 0.99 (none / Rev H re-tuned / oracle). At 4-6 Hz: none 803, Rev H re-tuned 835, oracle 40 um.
text.implication: The +-3 mm nose has the reach for 1-2 mm tremor; the tremor tracker, not the mechanism, limits the benefit, and it barely acts below about 6 Hz
text.weighted_headline: +60 g: ink error x1.20 at 8-10 Hz and x1.08 at 4-6 Hz vs the 12 g pen (1-2 mm); see et_sensitivity for the stiff-grip case

text.headline: x-height end of line (start 5.0 mm): off 4.19, cue 5.18, lines 4.85, size assist x1.35 5.58, vertical adaptive 5.22 mm; tremor in ink off 124 vs x1.35 165 um; jerk off 239 vs x1.35 595; letters touching 12% vs 50%
text.implication: If people respond to a cue as assumed (PDT-19), a vibration cue keeps letters at their start size for about 11 % more writing time; lines >= 1 cm halve the shrinkage; a fixed size gain only rescales the shrinking letters and enlarges tremor, jerk and (horizontally) crowding; an adaptive vertical gain restores the size with little ink cost but hides the deficit from the writer: test it against lines and the cue for agency, after-effects and fluency (EXP-HW3)

labels.cue: Buzz on a wrong letter (the ink is not changed)
labels.nose_nogate: Nose guidance with no limits (the pen would write for you)

text.headline: Dysgraphia-like: ink vs target none 582 um, nose full 225, board full 384; letters read 0.92 / 0.86 / 0.85; device share 38% (nose) and 25% (board). Dyslexia-like: reversed or wrong letters read as the target: none 0.00, nose full 0.00; cue flags 100% of errors
text.implication: Guidance brings the ink closer to the copybook target during guidance, but the device then authors 20-40 % of the ink motion; full guidance leaves hybrid letters that are read less well, partial nose guidance keeps them readable; no guidance turns a reversed or wrong letter into the right one, so for dyslexia the app's flagging against a known target carries the benefit. Only unassisted retention tests can show learning (HAP-41..44; EXP-HW4)
